lead: More than 34 museums and cultural centres, from Spain’s second-largest art gallery to the best immersive exhibitions. Valencia’s cultural agenda never stops all year.

Valencia has one of the most active cultural scenes in Spain. From the country’s second-largest art gallery at the Museo de Bellas Artes to the international contemporary art of the Hortensia Herrero Centre, by way of the great immersive exhibitions of the Fundación Bancaja. Most municipal museums are free, and the big private centres offer top-level programmes all year round.
Here you will find Valencia’s main exhibition spaces with their permanent collections, opening hours and up-to-date prices.

items.title: IVAM · Institut Valencià d’Art Modern
items.subtitle: The benchmark for modern and contemporary art in Valencia
items.body: The Valencian Institute of Modern Art is the city’s cultural reference for 20th- and 21st-century art. Founded in 1989 as the first modern art museum in Spain, it houses the largest collection of works by the sculptor Julio González and programmes temporary exhibitions by top national and international artists.
facts: The world’s largest collection by the avant-garde Valencian sculptor
Works by Picasso, Calder, Lichtenstein and great modern masters
Temporary exhibitions with artists from the current international scene
C/ de Guillem de Castro, 118 · El Carmen district

items.title: Museo de Bellas Artes de Valencia (Fine Arts Museum)
items.subtitle: Spain’s second most important art gallery
items.body: The Museo de Bellas Artes de Valencia houses the second most important painting collection in Spain after the Prado. It occupies a former 17th-century college next to the Turia Gardens and its collection runs from medieval Valencian art to Impressionism. Sorolla, Ribalta, Joan de Joanes and the Valencian Primitives are the great protagonists.
facts: The largest public collection of paintings by Joaquín Sorolla outside the Sorolla Museum in Madrid
Joan de Joanes and the great masters of 15th-century Valencian Gothic
The master of Valencian tenebrism in his full historical context
C/ de Sant Pius V, 9 · Turia Gardens
Free · Open access all year round

items.title: Centre del Carme Cultura Contemporánea
items.subtitle: Current art in a 13th-century Gothic convent
items.body: The Centre del Carme is a unique cultural space: a former 13th-century Carmelite convent converted into a contemporary art centre by the Consorci de Museus of the Generalitat Valenciana. Its Gothic cloisters and stone rooms are the perfect setting for photography exhibitions, installations, street art and works by emerging and established artists.
facts: Exhibitions by local and national artists in unique historic spaces
Seasons dedicated to documentary photography and street art
The space is heritage in itself: a 13th-century cloister with integrated exhibitions
C/ del Museu, 2 · El Carmen district
Free · Permanent and temporary exhibitions open to all

items.title: Centro de Arte Hortensia Herrero
items.subtitle: International art in a 17th-century palace
items.body: Opened in 2023 in the Palacio Valeriola, a fully restored 17th-century building, the Centro de Arte Hortensia Herrero houses one of the most important private contemporary art collections in Spain. Works by Andreas Gursky, Anselm Kiefer, Georg Baselitz, Anish Kapoor and Mat Collishaw sit alongside archaeological remains of a Roman circus, a medieval Jewish quarter and an Islamic fountain.
facts: Gursky, Kiefer, Baselitz, Kapoor: great names of international art
Traces of the Roman circus, medieval Jewish quarter and Islamic fountain underground
Works by top international artists in constant rotation
Paid admission · Check price on the website

items.title: Fundación Bancaja
items.subtitle: Major temporary exhibitions in the heart of the city
items.body: The Fundación Bancaja is the benchmark cultural centre for Valencia’s major temporary exhibitions. With an annual programme that combines classical art, photography, science and popular culture, it has hosted shows on Sorolla in immersive format, ancient Egypt with Tutankhamun and other large-scale exhibitions that attract hundreds of thousands of visitors.
facts: International touring shows of high visual and cultural impact
Multisensory experiences with large-scale technology and projections
Educational programme and cultural activities alongside each exhibition

items.title: CaixaForum Valencia
items.subtitle: Europe’s largest vertical garden + top-level art
items.body: CaixaForum Valencia occupies the Àgora of the City of Arts and Sciences and has the largest vertical garden in Europe on its outer façade. A versatile cultural space with international art exhibitions, lecture series, concerts and family workshops. It has a bookshop and a restaurant with views of the complex’s lake. Access to the building is free; the exhibitions require a ticket.
facts: Contemporary art, science and photography from collections around the world
Europe’s largest vertical garden on the building’s outer façade
Educational workshops for children and families every weekend
Av. del Professor López Piñero · City of Arts and Sciences
Free access to the building · Exhibitions require a ticket

items.title: MuVIM · Museu Valencià de la Il·lustració i la Modernitat
items.subtitle: The history of modern thought in images
items.body: The Museu Valencià de la Il·lustració i la Modernitat is the only museum in Spain devoted to modern thought and the Enlightenment. Its exhibition programme covers the history of graphic design, contemporary architecture, street art, pop culture and Valencian traditions, in exhibitions that combine historical rigour with attractive visual proposals.
facts: The only collection devoted to the history of modern thought in Spain
Exhibitions on graffiti, graphic design and contemporary visual culture
Shows on the traditions, festivals and intangible heritage of Valencia

items.title: Museo Nacional de Cerámica · Palacio Marqués de Dos Aguas
items.subtitle: Spain’s most exuberant Baroque turned into a museum
items.body: The Palacio del Marqués de Dos Aguas is one of the most exuberant Baroque buildings in Spain, with an 18th-century alabaster-carved doorway that leaves every visitor open-mouthed. Inside, the Museo Nacional de Cerámica houses one of the most important ceramics collections in the world, with pieces from Moorish times to the present day.
facts: The 18th-century Baroque façade, one of the most impressive in Spain
A collection from Moorish tiles to 20th-century Manises pieces
Furniture, textiles and sumptuary objects from different historical periods
C/ del Poeta Querol, 2 · Historic centre
Free on Saturday afternoons and Sundays · €3 other times

items.title: The Legend of the Titanic
items.body: Period objects, real history and immersive art to feel like a passenger on the most famous ocean liner in history.

items.title: La Ruta · Modernity, culture and excess
items.body: The Valencian “Ruta del Bakalao” revisited as a cultural phenomenon: art, photography, fashion and music with interactive elements.

items.title: Leonardo. 500 years of genius
items.body: The machines and inventions of Leonardo da Vinci in exhibition format at the Museu de les Ciències until April 2026.

items.title: Temporary IVAM exhibitions
items.body: The IVAM programmes 8–10 temporary exhibitions a year by international artists. Check the up-to-date programme at ivam.es.

blocks.title: Tips for visiting museums and exhibitions in Valencia
items: The Museo de Bellas Artes is free all year round and has the best Sorolla paintings with free access
The IVAM, the Centre del Carme and the MuVIM are free: perfect for a museum day on no budget
The Fundación Bancaja hosts the big seasonal exhibitions: book in advance
The Centro Hortensia Herrero has limited capacity: buy your ticket online before you go
Municipal museums close on Mondays: plan your visit carefully
CaixaForum is open every day of the year, including public holidays, with free access to the building
